answer: The maker files the gear teeth to a pattern only he knows, and the escapement's signature is recorded when the clock is sold. A relic movement bought from another shop fails: at the nectar of the teeth the file marks must match the maker's own pattern, and bought gears carry another hand. Forging the pattern takes a watchmaker, 180 practice movements and 11,700 in fees, while the garden signature in the guild book is kept for life, so a second clock with the same teeth is seized.
